title: One peptide hinge, many moving atoms
topic:
Create exactly one self-contained, visual-first scene about a local peptide torsion. This is a standalone pipeline demonstration, with no existing lesson or selection to assume. Use subtitle-only delivery: concise connected explanatory text (roughly 35-45 words), no speech audio, no title screen or recap. Target about 16-22 seconds; obey the actual subtitle timing packet rather than a hardcoded duration. Reserve a clear initial setup and a final reading hold. Optional captions are delivery metadata, not text panels in the animation.

The following custom visual directions refine the desired operation and take precedence over their illustrative exact timestamps: 
Create one original 16-second silent visual explanation: **one local backbone torsion reorients the downstream peptide while bond lengths and upstream structure remain unchanged**. Use the actual animlib APIs and the documented atomic-peptide recipe, including its explicit small component template. Use 5–7 residues with stable atom and residue IDs; do not invent sequence-to-fold or imported-structure APIs. Keep the same molecular object throughout.

The molecule owns the frame. Compose a large, obliquely viewed atomic stick construction on near-black, with thin clean bonds, modest atom dots and generous empty space around the hinge's sweep. Use a fixed camera during setup, action and result so stationary upstream atoms visibly remain stationary. Pre-fit the complete motion in one common coordinate frame; do not subtract the pose's changing center. Do not add a grid, title panel, cards, footer narration, realistic surface, glow, or decorative camera movement.

Use neutral or muted blue for the retained upstream structure, teal for the selected middle N–C-alpha rotation axis, and orange for the downstream moving portion. These are pedagogical role colors, not chemical element colors, and stay stable. Show short local leaders identifying N and C-alpha on the hinge only. All visible bonds must come from the returned explicit bond list; all atom positions come from `s.peptidePose`. Make the selected residue a middle residue with index greater than zero: changing phi[0] does not articulate this builder's first residue. Change exactly one middle phi; hold all other phi and psi entries fixed. Choose a moderate rotation and an oblique view that make the sweep clearly visible without self-occlusion.

Suggested timing: 0–2 seconds establish the readable chain; 2–4 seconds emphasize the hinge and its local phi label and retain a faint initial copy of only the moving portion; 4–9 seconds ease the single torsion through its sweep; 9–12 seconds hold the endpoint. During motion retain one clearly identified downstream atom and reveal its geometrically correct circular arc about the hinge axis. Keep the faint original pose available to compare. At the endpoint briefly emphasize one unchanged bond segment with a nearby small length mark, so the invariant is visible rather than asserted by a caption. From 12–16 seconds hold the earned configuration with the retained original, axis and arc readable; allow only a quiet local final label such as “same bonds” if useful. No reset, recap card or second unrelated mechanism.

Use restrained local serif/math text at native-readable scale. Put phi beside its actual axis. If an angle value is displayed, compute it from the same torsion input; if arc geometry is shown, derive its center/radius/plane from the selected atom and fixed N–C-alpha axis, not from an arbitrary screen-space circle. Labels and leaders must share the molecule's static world transform. Keep the light ghost substantially quieter than the current chain. Give the viewer a clear initial hold and at least two seconds to inspect the result. This is a schematic prescribed torsion, not folding dynamics or an energetic prediction.

Do not import or copy a preauthored scene. Produce the scene through the real generation pipeline using the provided authoring reference and capabilities. Favor simple public APIs and explicit bounded arrays over unnecessary infrastructure.

Use six residues and exactly one middle phi angle change; do not turn this into whole-protein folding. No interactive controls or viewer orbit are needed. Preserve the scientific caveat in concise explanatory text: the torsion is prescribed, not a folding simulation. Produce entirely new source through the pipeline, not a copied demo.
